clue.text: Paper finished? Stop working!

parts.note: The Times is the newspaper in which this very puzzle appears
up as in 'time is up', meaning over or ended

explanation.surface: A journalist hears that the paper has folded and is told to down tools.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and exclamation suggest a newsroom drama; the first half is the wordplay and the shout is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the invigilator's call telling candidates their allotted period has ended and they must put pens down.

clue.text: Worker taken from pool, perhaps, getting unusually tipsy after short time

indicators.note: after puts the rearranged letters following the abbreviation for time

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters of tipsy are arranged in an unusual order

explanation.surface: An office worker drawn from a pool of staff gets oddly drunk after a brief period.
explanation.walkthrough: A typing pool was a shared office room of typists, so 'taken from pool' is not swimming; 'unusually' scrambles the drunk word to YPIST, set 'after' the time abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Typists were often drawn from a firm's typing pool, a shared group of clerical workers, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Maiden appearing shortly in rainy season

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
on means appearing, as a performer is on stage
soon means shortly

explanation.surface: A young woman is about to show up during the wet season.
explanation.walkthrough: M for maiden is a cricket scoring abbreviation (an over with no runs).
explanation.definitionFit: In South Asia the season of heavy seasonal rains brought by the shifting wind is known by this name.

clue.text: Cutting device into which writing implement goes? Right

definitions.text: Cutting device into which writing implement goes? Right

indicators.note: into which says the writing tool is placed inside the blade's name

parts.note: a share, as in ploughshare, is the cutting blade of a plough
a pen is an implement for writing

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a pencil goes into a cutting gadget, and is told it does.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a pencil sharpener is a cutting device a writing implement goes into. 'goes' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A pencil sharpener has a blade that shaves wood as the pencil is turned in its hole, so it is a cutting device.

clue.text: Cut new academic work that's the next thing here

parts.note: to pare is to trim or cut
a thesis is a dissertation written for a degree

explanation.surface: Instructions to trim a new dissertation, followed by a remark about what comes next.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points at the bracket holding the letter count, (11), which comes straight after the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The enumeration printed after the clue sits inside round brackets, a bracketed aside, so the next thing is literally one.

clue.text: Farm animal was found with horse or bull

parts.note: a hog is a pig, a farmyard beast
H is slang for heroin, which is also called horse

explanation.surface: A pig turns up beside a horse or a bull, as in a farmyard inventory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' looks like another farm animal but stands for heroin, slang H; 'bull' looks like a third beast but is the definition, nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Bull, short for a coarser word, is slang for nonsense or rubbish talk, just like this word.

clue.text: Part of skirt that may attract attention

definitions.meaning: the turned-up and stitched lower edge of a garment
a little cough or 'ahem' made to catch someone's notice

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a garment's folded border and also the throat-clearing sound used to get noticed.

clue.text: Russian writer turns on left

parts.note: two goes or turns, a go being a turn in a game

explanation.surface: A Russian author rounds on the political left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' gives GO twice (goes, turns in a game), and 'on' links with L after them.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikolai Gogol, author of Dead Souls and The Overcoat, was a nineteenth-century Russian novelist and dramatist.

clue.text: Surrounded by feelings of dread, doctor is brought in

indicators.note: brought in says the doctor's letters are put inside the word for dread

parts.note: angst is anxiety or dread
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A frightened patient, gripped by dread, has a doctor called in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in' signals the container; MO, medical officer, is a common crossword doctor, and the definition is the opening preposition, not the feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: The preposition means in the middle of or surrounded by others, as in 'amongst friends'.

clue.text: Pile -has something small and sharp and unknown inside?

indicators.note: inside says the unknown letter goes within the word has

parts.note: taken as written
Y is an algebraic unknown
a tack is a small sharp nail

explanation.surface: A heap that may conceal something tiny and pointed, recalling the needle proverb.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the proverbial needle hidden in a pile of hay; 'inside' signals the algebraic unknown going within the verb, with the small nail following.
explanation.definitionFit: A stack of hay is a large pile of it, so the specific heap stands for the general word.

clue.text: Write sign on label, a magical symbol

indicators.note: on, in an across answer, puts the zodiac sign after the label, as if attached to its end

parts.note: to pen is to write
a tag is a label
the Ram, Aries, is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Instructions to write a star sign on a label, producing an occult emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the sign after the label in this across answer; 'sign' is a zodiac sign, the Ram.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-pointed star drawn in one continuous line is used as a symbol in magic and the occult.

clue.text: Hero's expression of delight

definitions.meaning: the good guy in a story, opposite of the baddy

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an informal noun for a story's virtuous character and a childlike cry of pleasure.

clue.text: Back one form of gambling in ship

indicators.note: back here means the word for this gambling game is read from its end to its start

parts.note: the football pools, a British betting game predicting match results

explanation.surface: Someone places a bet aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like 'bet on' in a gambling surface, but it turns POOLS round; the pools are a British football-results betting game.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-masted sailing vessel is a kind of ship, so the specific boat stands for the general word.

clue.text: Source of illumination one badly needed, left in dark

indicators.note: in tells us the scrambled word plus the letter go inside the word for darkness

parts.note: night is the dark time

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of the small word one are put in a poor, disordered arrangement

explanation.surface: A lamp is desperately wanted by someone stuck in darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges ONE to EON; with L that goes 'in' NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas-discharge tube glowing red is a lamp, a thing that gives off illumination.

clue.text: Bad smell rising — fish smell —- past its sell-by date?

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the letters of the body odour abbreviation read upwards

parts.note: BO is body odour
sole is a flatfish
a scent is a smell

explanation.surface: A rotten stench, a fishy odour: surely the food is out of date?
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns BO upwards in this down answer to OB.
explanation.definitionFit: Something going out of date or becoming outmoded is on its way out, like goods past the sell-by date, hence the query.

clue.text: Thus ennui acts — I could become apathetic

indicators.note: could become signals that the letters of the words before it can be turned into a different word

explanation.surface: Bored by such tedious acts, the speaker admits they might grow listless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could become' rearranges all fourteen letters of THUS ENNUI ACTS I.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking enthusiasm or interest is exactly what being apathetic means, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Water a mother pig

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
swine is a pig

explanation.surface: A farmyard listing of water, a mother and a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam's wine (or ale) is a jocular name for water, the only drink Adam had.
explanation.definitionFit: The humorous phrase names plain water, said to be the only drink available to the first man in Eden.

clue.text: Used by writer, it gives no impression of character

definitions.text: Used by writer, it gives no impression of character

parts.words: Used by writer, it gives no impression of character
parts.note: a typist's keyboard key that prints no letter, only a gap, read as if about a dull personality

explanation.surface: A writer's tool that leaves no mark of personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' means a personality but here a typed letter; 'impression' is a printed mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The long bar on a keyboard inserts a blank between words, printing no letter or symbol at all.

clue.text: Political group in power, with margin increased by miles

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for power
a rim is an edge or margin
rose means went up or increased
a league is an old measure of about three miles

explanation.surface: A party in government whose majority has grown by miles.
explanation.walkthrough: The Primrose League was a British Conservative organisation founded in 1883 in memory of Disraeli; 'margin' and 'increased' read like election talk.
explanation.definitionFit: It was a Victorian Conservative movement promoting Tory principles, so it counts as a political organisation.

clue.text: Temporarily appointed, I'm put in grave situation initially

indicators.note: situation initially says the burial word is positioned at the start, ahead of the contraction

parts.note: to inter is to bury

explanation.surface: Someone appointed for a while laments being placed in a serious predicament at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave situation' reads as a crisis, but 'put in grave' means bury, and 'situation initially' puts that first.
explanation.definitionFit: An interim officer holds a post provisionally until a permanent holder is found, so is temporarily appointed.

clue.text: Person speaking as absolute monarch

parts.note: utter means absolute or complete
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone talking in the manner of an all-powerful ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absolute monarch' looks like one phrase, a despot, but splits in two; ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen.
explanation.definitionFit: One who utters words is a speaker, so the agent noun formed from the verb means a person speaking.

clue.text: Couple working together in text and -e-mail

indicators.note: in shows the answer lies inside the run of letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A pair cooperate by text message and email.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'text' through 'and' into 'e-mail'.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people working in tandem act jointly, as on a bicycle built for two, so they are a cooperating pair.

clue.text: Emotional release is beyond heretical group

indicators.note: beyond places the little word is after the name of the sect in the answer

parts.note: the Cathars were a medieval Christian sect condemned as heretics; the group is the sect named in the plural

explanation.surface: A remark that cathartic feeling lies outside the reach of some heretics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beyond' signals that the little verb comes after the sect; the Cathars were a medieval heretical movement in southern France, crushed in the Albigensian Crusade.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek-derived term names the purging of pent-up feelings, an emotional release, as through tragedy or therapy.

clue.text: From a large number of Indians, heard expression of regret

indicators.note: heard tells us the phrase is spoken, giving a word with the same pronunciation

parts.note: a lakh is the Indian term for one hundred thousand, so this is 'a lakh'

explanation.surface: Someone among a crowd of Indians is heard lamenting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indians' suggests people, but a lakh is the Indian-English word for 100,000; 'From' links.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic exclamation of sorrow, usually paired as 'alas and', expresses regret.

clue.text: Source of wood in kit as ordered

indicators.note: ordered signals the letters of the two words kit and as are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Timber arrives in a kit, just as it was ordered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' looks like a link but is fodder: 'ordered' rearranges KIT AS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sitka spruce, named after an Alaskan town, is a tree widely grown for timber, hence a wood source.

clue.text: With major difficulty, returned parent to old country

indicators.note: returned means the word for the snag is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a rub is a snag or difficulty, as in 'there's the rub'
ma is mother, a parent

explanation.surface: After great hardship, a mother or father goes back to their homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns the snag word round to BUR; 'there's the rub' (Hamlet) gives the difficulty. The old country is Myanmar's former name.
explanation.definitionFit: Myanmar was called by this name until 1989, so it is a country under its former title.

clue.text: Break-up of empire left-winger initially staged

indicators.note: break-up signals the letters of empire are split apart and reassembled

parts.note: a red is a socialist or communist, someone on the political left

explanation.surface: An empire collapses as a radical leftist takes charge first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks like a first-letter signal for 'left-winger', but it belongs to the definition: first staged.
explanation.definitionFit: A play or film is said to have opened in this way when it is performed or shown for the first time.

clue.text: Criticise all in many words, initially

definitions.meaning: to slate or savage a performance in a review
the Greek-derived prefix meaning all, found at the start of words like panorama

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb meaning to review harshly, and also the prefix meaning all that begins pandemic and panacea.

clue.text: Stuff English family assembled in dish

parts.note: to ram is to cram or stuff
kin are one's relatives or family

explanation.surface: An English family gathers to stuff themselves from a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' reads as a noun or as eating, but it is the verb cram.
explanation.definitionFit: A small ceramic baking pot for one serving, as for soufflés, is a kind of dish.

clue.text: More excited by article showing mathematical achievement

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: excited signals the letters of the word more are stirred into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A news article reporting a mathematical breakthrough makes readers more thrilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More excited' reads as an emotional comparison, but 'excited' scrambles the four letters to OREM, which follows the article.
explanation.definitionFit: A proven mathematical proposition is something a mathematician achieves by proof, like Fermat's last.
